Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Aegis CyberTech Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question queue will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aegis CyberTech's results for the second quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Security Officer; and Rachel Kim, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Aegis CyberTech continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about Aegis One and the resulting acceleration in expansions and renewals is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: driving superior net dollar retention through expansions and retention; maximizing channel partner performance and their revenue contributions; minimizing churn through proactive customer success; providing clear next quarter billings guidance amid strong demand; mitigating the impact of currency fluctuations on our international revenue; and incorporating customer feedback on new products and features to fuel innovation.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $234.1 million, representing a 24% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 88% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 77%, while operating expenses were $150.2 million. Net income was $42.5 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.48. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Let me dive deeper into some key metrics starting with net dollar retention, or NDR, which is the gold standard for SaaS businesses like ours in cybersecurity. It captures customer stickiness and our ability to expand within our existing base, calculated as the ratio of dollar-based revenue retained from customers at the start of the period—after expansions, upsells, cross-sells, downgrades, and churn—relative to starting monthly recurring revenue.

In Q2, we delivered an NDR of 118%, up 300 basis points sequentially from 115% in Q1 and 8 percentage points year-over-year from 110% in Q2 FY2023. This is our 11th straight quarter above 115%, far exceeding the median for public cybersecurity peers around 105-110%. Our cohort analysis shows customers onboarded three years ago now generate 145% of their original annual contract value through natural expansion, thanks to our modular Aegis One architecture.

Breaking it down: gross dollar retention excluding downsells was 98%, with just 2% net revenue contraction from pricing or scope changes—well below the industry average of 5-7% amid economic pressures. Dollar churn was a low 4.2%, mainly from a few small SMB accounts in non-core areas like retail, influenced by budget scrutiny following incidents like the CrowdStrike outage. Our enterprise cohort with over $1 million ARR had zero dollar churn for the fifth straight quarter, supported by multi-year contracts averaging 36 months and 95% renewal rates.

Expansion drove 24% of the NDR uplift, with $28 million in net expansion revenue, up 35% year-over-year: 12% from upsells like scaling Endpoint Detection and Response from 500 to 5,000 seats as hybrid work normalized; 8% from cross-sells into Zero Trust Network Access and Secure Access Service Edge bundles, now 42% of large-deal ACV; and 4% from land-and-expand, such as Cloud Workload Protection growing into full-stack Extended Detection and Response.

This is powered by Aegis One's native integrations and AI capabilities. Our GenAI-powered Threat Hunting module, launched last Q4, achieved 15% attachment rates among EDR users, boosting mean contract value 2.5x. Partnerships with hyperscalers helped: AWS Marketplace expansions added $12 million in upsells, and our Azure Sentinel co-sell program saw 28% adoption, using our Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response playbooks to automate 40% of incidents.

Regionally: North America at 65% of ARR delivered 120% NDR, driven by CISA's Zero Trust Maturity Model and demand after the Change Healthcare ransomware. EMEA reached 116% from 112%, aided by NIS2 deadlines and 22% cross-sell penetration for Data Loss Prevention among GDPR customers. APAC at 18% of ARR hit 112%, up from 105%, with Managed Detection and Response up 45% YoY in Japan and India amid state-sponsored threats and data sovereignty rules.

These trends affirm our platformization strategy in a fragmented market. Expansions yield 95% gross margins versus 75% for new logos, creating a flywheel where customers consolidate vendors, cutting total cost of ownership 30-40% via our AI-orchestrated Extended Security Posture Management. We're aiming for 120%+ NDR in FY2025 by pushing SASE+AI bundles and entering the $15 billion OT/IoT market with ICS protection, drawing from Colonial Pipeline lessons.

Next, our channel partners are a critical growth engine. They drove 65% of total revenue at $152.3 million, up from 58% last year and 62% in Q1—a 28% YoY increase outpacing overall growth. Trailing 12-month channels are 63% of $892 million ARR, with channel net revenue retention at 128% from upsells in AegisXDR and CloudShield SASE.

Top-tier platinum and gold partners like TD Synnex, Ingram Micro, and Arrow accounted for 42% of channel bookings or $64 million; TD Synnex grew 35% YoY pushing AegisXDR into mid-market finance with $450K average ACV, up 15%, via $12 million in market development funds for zero-trust campaigns.

MSP and MSSP ecosystem shone at 18% or $27.4 million, up 42% YoY. Partners like ConnectWise and Kaseya embedded our MDR, with 1,200 MSPs certified via Partner Enablement Portal. Our MSP Accelerator integrates API-first XDR with RMM tools, cutting time-to-value from 90 to 45 days and boosting pipeline velocity 55%. AegisXDR 6.2 adds AI behavioral analytics against phishing kits.

Hyperscalers at 5% generated $7.6 million, up 67% YoY via AWS and Azure Marketplaces with Bring Your Own License for edge SASE. Fifteen new AWS pursuits target healthcare HIPAA needs post-Change Healthcare.

North America at 72% of channel revenue or $109.7 million grew 31% via VARs like CDW with FedRAMP and CMMC wins; SMB ARR up 39%. EMEA at 16% or $24.4 million up 22% despite headwinds, via Westcoast and Bechtle for NIS2 SASE; Orange Cyberdefense bundle adds €15 million pipeline. APAC at 9% or $13.7 million up 45%, led by Singtel and Telstra; India MDR up 52% for UPI fraud. LATAM at 3% or $4.5 million up 38% via Ingram for Pix vulnerabilities.

We've added 450 net new partners YTD, 30% more, through CyberShield Alliance with up to 25% rebates and equity co-marketing. Partner360 Dashboard on Snowflake boosts pipeline 40%, close rates to 36% versus 28% direct. Channels anchor FY2024 revenue guidance of $975-1,005 million at 25-30% growth, targeting 68-70% mix with GenAI Guardrails for LLM defenses and hyperscaler depth in $212 billion market by 2027.

On churn, we track logo churn at 3.2% quarterly or 12% annualized—down 18% YoY and our best in two years—dollar churn at 2.1% offset by $18.7 million expansions, driving 118% NRR up 200 basis points sequentially, beating peers like Zscaler at 112%. This highlights AegisXDR stickiness.

Churn drivers from 450+ enterprise and 2,500+ mid-market analysis: 42% from M&A/consolidation like Broadcom-VMware, $4.2 million ARR mostly mid-market non-renewals; multi-year contracts limited damage. 28% macro/budget pressures, $3.1 million SMB hit in retail/manufacturing. 18% competitive losses to CrowdStrike EDR or Okta IAM, $2.8 million, but win-back at 22% via 40% lower TCO. 12% operational/support, $1.4 million from SIEM integrations; false positives addressed.

Regions: Americas 2.5% logo churn, NRR 122% via hyperscalers and CMMC. EMEA 4.1% from NIS2/UK headwinds. APAC 3.8% flat, Australia strong. Sequential improvement five quarters; enterprise sub-2%, mid-market 4.5% closing via plans. Expansions at 132% of prior ARR, 25% ZTNA attach.

Retention initiatives: Orion AI cuts MTTD 55%, false positives 42%; Unified XDR Fabric integrates 150+ tools, 15% upsell; Threat Hunting as-a-Service for 40% customers cuts operational churn 25%. FY25 goal sub-3% churn, 120%+ NRR via CSMs to 160, AI health scoring, 3-year escalators, M&A playbooks, vertical bundles cutting churn 22%.

For next quarter billings guidance into Q3 FY2024, we expect $260-275 million, sequential 11-17% growth from Q2's $235 million and 27-34% YoY. This reflects demand for AI-native solutions amid LockBit ransomware and AI attacks like Log4j/MOVEit.

Drivers: $50-55 million new ACV, 24% YoY, ACV per customer $1.1 million up 17% via EDR/CWP/SWG bundles; NRR 122% with 40% ADEM attach. GenAI Threat Intelligence with 98% MITRE accuracy converts 85% pilots, $12 million billings; SASE 2.0 SSE for shadow IT.

Regions: Americas 72% mix 14-19% growth via AWS/Azure banks. EMEA 18% 19-24% on NIS2. APAC 10% 24-29% via NTT/Telstra. Consumption pricing 44% new ACV, $1.2 billion cRPO up 31%; margins to 27-29%. Risks: federal delays, sales cycles 7-8 months, but $1.3 billion pipeline 4.1x coverage.

Currency fluctuations impacted Q2 revenue by $18 million headwind or 1.8%, mainly stronger USD; constant currency growth was 26% versus reported 24%. International 52% mix: Americas 45% $105 million, EMEA 35% $82 million, APAC 20% $47 million.

EMEA $10 million hit from EUR -6.8% and GBP -4.5% on ECB cuts/Brexit; constant 30% YoY on NIS2 like Prisma Access. APAC $6 million from JPY -11%, AUD -4.7%; constant 27% on zero-trust. LATAM $2 million BRL/CAD.

Hedging covers 78% 2024 exposure, 62% Q3 at 1.09 USD/EUR, 142 JPY/USD; mitigated from $26 million potential. Dynamic pricing in Aegis Guardian XDR preserves 82% power; shifting to North America, JPY contracts. Q3 headwind $12-16 million; constant 25-27% FY growth.

Customer feedback on new products is stellar, from VoC on 4,000+ clients: NPS 76 up 24% YoY, top Gartner quartile; QuantumXDR CSAT 91%, 87% praise AI analytics. 43% top enterprises migrated in three months, 27% QoQ expansion.

GenAI Threat Hunter on 14 petabytes cuts MTTD 65% for APTs; U.S. bank neutralized LockBit, cut alert fatigue 53%. ShieldEdge ZTNA eBPF sub-50ms latency, 91% renewal, 34% DLP attach, ACV up 21%.

North America 57% new revenue NPS 81, SEC/NIST automation. EMEA 40% ramp NIS2 Attack Path Mapping. APAC 51% growth PDPA sovereign clouds, 72% shadow IT cut; India integrations patched.

Platformization: 3.1x NRR at 127%, 61% land-and-expand $420K uplift. Q3 betas NPS 83 for post-quantum crypto. Expect 24-29% new ARR growth.

Dr. Lena Patel: Thank you, Mike. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing our GenAI Threat Intelligence and Orion AI Engine for faster MTTD, unifying our XDR Fabric with 150+ integrations, and rolling out quantum-resistant features to counter emerging nation-state threats, all informed by customer feedback and cohort expansions.

Tom Hargrove: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape—from ransomware like LockBit to supply chain risks like SolarWinds—and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with 99.99% SOC uptime and proactive hunting services.

Rachel Kim: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, expanding channel partnerships like our CyberShield Alliance and hyperscaler alliances to reach a wider audience, with pipeline up 41% and close rates improving.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star then 1 if you would like to ask a question. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, could you expand on the NDR components and churn drivers, especially enterprise versus mid-market trends?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Ben. Mike covered the details well, but to reiterate, our 118% NDR reflects robust expansions at 24% contribution, with zero enterprise dollar churn and expansions like ZTNA cross-sells fueling it. Churn at 3.2% logo is down YoY, driven by M&A and budgets but offset by our initiatives like Orion AI reclaiming at-risk ARR. Enterprise sub-2% shows the moat, and we're closing the mid-market gap with tailored plans.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. On channels and FX—how much did currency headwinds mask channel strength, and what's the outlook for partner mix?

Mike Chen: Hi Lisa. Channels at 65% overdelivered with 28% YoY growth despite $18 million FX drag, constant currency even stronger at 27%. EMEA and APAC hit hard by EUR/JPY, but hedging and pricing preserved margins. Targeting 68-70% mix by year-end with new partners and GenAI bundles, resilient given $2.1 billion backlog.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Thanks. CTO, customer feedback on GenAI features and XDR—any quantifiable impact on adoption and expansions?

Dr. Lena Patel: Thanks, Raj. Feedback is outstanding with NPS 76 and 92% CSAT on QuantumXDR's GenAI Hunter cutting MTTD 65% and fatigue 53%, driving 43% enterprise migration and 27% expansion. SASE ZTNA latency wins add 34% attach; betas for post-quantum at NPS 83 position us for 135% dollar expansion in $12 billion XDR market.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez: Congrats team. Mike or Tom, thoughts on Q3 billings guide and any risks from macro or threats?

Tom Hargrove: Thanks, Emily. Mike's $260-275 million guide embeds 11-17% sequential via new ACV and regions like APAC 24-29%. Risks like federal budgets mitigated by 4.1x pipeline and consumption shift; threat escalation from Lazarus actually tailwinds zero-trust demand, aligning with our SOC and hunting focus.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
